reason: The text contains multiple regular people characters with clear dialogue, emotions, and opinions. The sailors demonstrate fear (וַיִּֽירְא֣וּ - 'they feared greatly'), speak to one another in decision-making (וַיֹּאמְר֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵ֗הוּ - 'they said to one another'), and express opinions about their situation. The captain speaks with Jonah (וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ - 'and he said to him'). The people of Nineveh demonstrate emotions through belief and repentance (וַֽיַּאֲמִ֛ינוּ אַנְשֵׁ֥י נִֽינְוֵ֖ה - 'the men of Nineveh believed'). Even Jonah himself is a regular person character exhibiting emotions throughout: fear, anger (וַיֵּ֥רַע אֶל־ יוֹנָ֖ה רָעָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה - 'it displeased Jonah greatly'), gladness, and despair.
